name: SPANISH 21
description: Spanish 21 (known internationally as Pontoon in Australia, not UK classic Pontoon) is a variant of Blackjack played with 'Spanish' decks (48 cards, removing the 10s). The removal of 10s increases the house edge, but this is compensated by extremely player-friendly rules such as 'Player 21 always wins', 'Surrender after Double', and special bonus payouts for specific 21 combinations (6-7-8, 7-7-7). It is highly popular in casinos.

content.text: Spanish 21 (known internationally as Pontoon in Australia, not UK classic Pontoon) is a variant of Blackjack played with 'Spanish' decks (48 cards, removing the 10s). The removal of 10s increases the house edge, but this is compensated by extremely player-friendly rules such as 'Player 21 always wins', 'Surrender after Double', and special bonus payouts for specific 21 combinations (6-7-8, 7-7-7). It is highly popular in casinos.
Introduced in Nevada casinos in 1995 by Masque Publishing. Based on the lack of 10s which favors the house.
One to seven players at the table, each playing independently against the dealer. Standard blackjack layout; six or eight Spanish decks in a shoe.
Standard Blackjack deal. 2 cards each. Dealer gets hole card.

items.text: Dealer stands on soft 17: House rule: dealer stands on soft 17. Lower house edge (about 0.40%).
Dealer hits soft 17: House rule: dealer hits soft 17. Redoubling allowed (up to three times) gives house edge about 0.42%; without redoubling about 0.76%.
